regions.notes: INV Anuario de Superficie 2024: 142,785 ha of vines (71.4% of national 199,946 ha; San Juan 39,684 ha). Other Mendoza crops (olive, stone fruit, garlic, vegetables) have no source read; MAGyP grain estimates show negligible field crops there.

countries.notes: National and provincial rankings computed from the MAGyP "Estimaciones agrícolas" open CSV (sown area, campaign 2023/2024, summed over departments; sub-categories such as soja 1ra/2da merged into totals). Dataset covers grains, oilseeds, pulses, cotton, rice, mate, tea only: sugar cane (last update 2004/05), citrus, potato, grapes, fruit and vegetables are NOT covered, so Tucumán (dataset shows soybean > maize > wheat > bean > chickpea, but sugar cane and lemon unsourced) was left out as a region. Oats and rye include area sown for forage/cover. National grape area 199,946 ha (INV 2024) would rank below the 8 listed. USDA IPAD (ipad.fas.usda.gov) returned HTTP 503 for every request.

countries.name: Brazil
countries.notes: IBGE Produção Agrícola Municipal (PAM) 2023, SIDRA table 5457 (https://sidra.ibge.gov.br/tabela/5457), variable 216 = harvested area (ha), temporary + permanent crops, read through the SIDRA API. Maize is the sum of 1st and 2nd crop as published. Coffee = arabica + canephora total.

countries.notes: Source: ODEPA "Fichas regionales" (PDFs, biblioteca digital ODEPA). The national ficha has no crop-area table, so the national ranking was DERIVED from the regional fichas: stated national totals (wine grapes 136,288.5 ha; annual crops 576,415 ha) and regional area divided by the published "% region/country" (approx.: wheat ~205k ha, grape ~182k incl. table grapes, oats ~97k, maize ~65k, potato ~44k, walnut ~43k, cherry ~39k, rapeseed ~38k). Data vintage is 2019-2021, i.e. older than the 2021 census; cherry and hazelnut have expanded since. INE census page reachable but had no crop tables in HTML; WebFetch to odepa.gob.cl failed on TLS (worked with curl).

countries.notes: INEI Compendio Estadístico Perú 2023, chapter 13 (data from MIDAGRI-DEIA). National ranking = harvested area 2022 (table 13.4); maize = amarillo duro 260,971 + amiláceo 199,729 + choclo 49,048 ha; coffee 423,854; rice 414,286; potato 341,468; alfalfa 209,284; cocoa 177,350; plantain 171,073; barley 127,932. The compendium gives no area by department, only production, hence the derived regional rankings (basis=production). MIDAGRI SIEA (siea.midagri.gob.pe) could not be reached (connection timeout / ECONNREFUSED).

countries.name: Colombia
countries.notes: UPRA / MinAgricultura "Evaluaciones Agropecuarias Municipales (EVA) 2019-2025, Base Agrícola" on datos.gov.co (dataset uejq-wxrr, https://www.datos.gov.co/d/uejq-wxrr), harvested area summed by department for year 2024 via the Socrata API. "Caña" merges sugar-mill cane and panela cane. In 2023 coffee (697,815 ha) ranked above rice (648,180 ha); in 2024 rice 679,091 vs coffee 671,192.

countries.name: Ecuador
countries.notes: Regions: MAG (SIPA) "Estadísticas agropecuarias de la provincia" 2024 bulletins, table "Principales cultivos" ordered by sown area, source INEC ESPAC 2024. Maize merges maíz duro and maíz suave (dry + choclo); banana includes orito. National: INEC ESPAC 2024 tabulados (T5 permanent, T8 transitory); I summed sub-columns (plantation age / seed type), so magnitudes are approximate (cocoa ~610k ha, palm ~200k, banana ~180k, plantain ~150k, sugar cane ~105k; rice and hard maize each roughly 275-400k) and the rice-vs-maize order is uncertain. Bulletins for Santo Domingo and Santa Elena returned 404 under the guessed file names. Planted pasture excluded.

countries.notes: WEAK SOURCING. Official MAG sites failed: can2022.mag.gov.py has an expired TLS certificate (not bypassed), dcea.mag.gov.py unreachable, www.mag.gov.py has no statistics links. National list is from a news article (La Nación PY, last-resort source) quoting CAN 2022: soybean 3,062,086 ha (normal) + >477,000 ha (zafriña); maize 229,120 + 963,090 ha (zafriña); irrigated rice 205,744; yerba mate 38,724; banana 15,960. Wheat, sugar cane and cassava are nationally important but no area figure was found, so they are omitted (wheat likely ranks 3rd). Regional figures come from the NGO report "Con la Soja al Cuello 2023" (BASE-IS), tables 2 and 4, built on CAN 2022 data: secondary source.

countries.notes: No official statistics found (no recent MPPAT/INE crop-area publication reachable). National list is from FEDEAGRO (producers' federation, NOT an official source) "Resultados 2025": maize ~293,400 ha (winter cycle), rice 148,000 ha (two cycles), coffee ~145,000 ha, oil palm ~80,000 ha, sugar cane ~63,000 ha (derived from 4.43 Mt at ~70 t/ha), potato ~9,400 ha, tomato ~6,750, onion ~6,600, soybean ~6,000. Cocoa, plantain/banana, cassava, sorghum and beans have no area in that source and are omitted. USDA IPAD returned HTTP 503; fas.usda.gov GAIN report page returned HTTP 403; FAOSTAT API returned 401.
